  8233	
  8234	The Fourier identities of the wave Green measures `G_s` in `d = 2, 3`,
  8235	Archimedes' law for Mathlib's sphere measure, and the extension of the
  8236	Green-smoothing identification of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` to every
  8237	`d = 1, 2, 3`, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/WaveGreenFourier.lean`.
  8238	Sources (`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`):
  8239	`G_s hat(xi) = sin(s norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, value `s` at `xi = 0` (lines
  8240	777-778, before `E:damped-norm-definitions`); the display
  8241	`G_h hat(xi) = sin(h norm(xi))/norm(xi)`, `G_h(R^d) = h` (lines 4740-4744, in
  8242	the proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`, lines 4702-4757), which the TeX quotes
  8243	from the source's (2.3)-(2.5), p. 7, without proof; the identity is also used
  8244	as `G_a hat` in `L:phase-contractions` (lines 2081-2084, 2107-2108, `d = 3`)
  8245	and in the proof of `L:alpha-one-convolution` (lines 4760-4818). The measures
  8246	are `WaveGreen.waveGreen` (unchanged): in `d = 3` the recorded definitional
  8247	choice `(s/(4 pi)) map (omega -> s omega) sigma` with `sigma = volume.toSphere`
  8248	(Le's decision 4 for wave L6); this module proves facts about that measure and
  8249	does not identify `sigma` with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure.

  8281	Proof route (the TeX has no proof; no Bessel functions). `d = 2`: rotate `xi`
  8282	to `norm(xi) e_0` by a reflection (Lebesgue measure is invariant under linear
  8283	isometries), slice along `x_0` (Fubini) and use
  8284	`int_(-a)^a (a^2 - u^2)^(-1/2) du = pi`. `d = 3`: compute
  8285	`int_(norm(x) < R) e^(i <xi,x>) dx` in polar coordinates
  8286	(`int_0^R r^2 Phi_xi(r) dr`, `Phi_xi(r) = int e^(i r <xi,omega>) sigma(d omega)`)
  8287	and by rotation and slicing (`pi int_(-R)^R (R^2 - t^2) e^(i norm(xi) t) dt`),
  8288	and differentiate both in `R` at `R = 1`; no rotation invariance of
  8289	`toSphere` is used (Mathlib has none). Archimedes: equality of characteristic
  8290	functions (`Measure.ext_of_charFun`). The definitions `splitFirst`
  8291	(`R^(n+1) = R x R^n`) and `spherePhi` (`Phi_xi`) only name route objects and
  8292	have no row.
  8293	
  8294	Hypotheses. Only `damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave` takes `H:homog`; it
  8295	uses `dim` directly and passes the hypothesis to
  8296	`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper` (fields as recorded
  8297	in `DampedMultiplier`). The Fourier identities and Archimedes' law are
  8298	statements about the measures alone (`d = 1, 2, 3`, `s > 0`, or `norm(e) = 1`).

   104	/-! ### Rotation and slicing -/
   105	/-- A linear isometry `ρ` of `ℝ^{n+1}` with `⟪ξ, ρx⟫ = ‖ξ‖ x₀` (the reflection
   106	exchanging `ξ` and `‖ξ‖e₀`, `Submodule.reflection_sub`).  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   107	theorem exists_rotation (n : ℕ) (ξ : Rd (n + 1)) :
   108	    ∃ ρ : Rd (n + 1) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Rd (n + 1), ∀ x, inner ℝ ξ (ρ x) = ‖ξ‖ * x 0 := by
   109	  set e0 : Rd (n + 1) := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 with he0
   110	  have hn : ‖ξ‖ = ‖‖ξ‖ • e0‖ := by simp [e0, norm_smul]
   111	  set K := (ℝ ∙ (ξ - ‖ξ‖ • e0))ᗮ
   112	  refine ⟨K.reflection, fun x => ?_⟩
   113	  have h1 : K.reflection ξ = ‖ξ‖ • e0 := Submodule.reflection_sub hn
   114	  calc inner ℝ ξ (K.reflection x)
   115	      = inner ℝ (K.reflection ξ) (K.reflection (K.reflection x)) :=
   116	        (K.reflection.inner_map_map _ _).symm
   117	    _ = ‖ξ‖ * x 0 := by
   118	        rw [Submodule.reflection_reflection, h1, real_inner_smul_left, he0,
   119	          EuclideanSpace.inner_single_left]
   120	        simp
   121	
   122	/-- Rotation: `∫ g(⟪ξ,x⟫, ‖x‖) dx = ∫ g(‖ξ‖x₀, ‖x‖) dx` on `ℝ^{n+1}` (Lebesgue
   123	measure is invariant under linear isometries; no integrability needed, both
   124	sides are Bochner integrals of functions exchanged by a measure-preserving
   125	equivalence).  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   126	theorem integral_inner_norm (n : ℕ) (ξ : Rd (n + 1)) (g : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) :
   127	    ∫ x : Rd (n + 1), g (inner ℝ ξ x) ‖x‖ = ∫ x : Rd (n + 1), g (‖ξ‖ * x 0) ‖x‖ := by
   128	  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ⟩ := exists_rotation n ξ
   129	  rw [← ρ.measurePreserving.integral_comp ρ.toHomeomorph.toMeasurableEquiv.measurableEmbedding
   130	    (fun x => g (inner ℝ ξ x) ‖x‖)]
   131	  simp [hρ]

   133	/-- Integrability form of `integral_inner_norm`.  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   134	theorem integrable_inner_norm (n : ℕ) (ξ : Rd (n + 1)) (g : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) :
   135	    Integrable (fun x : Rd (n + 1) => g (inner ℝ ξ x) ‖x‖) ↔
   136	      Integrable (fun x : Rd (n + 1) => g (‖ξ‖ * x 0) ‖x‖) := by
   137	  obtain ⟨ρ, hρ⟩ := exists_rotation n ξ
   138	  rw [← ρ.measurePreserving.integrable_comp_emb
   139	    ρ.toHomeomorph.toMeasurableEquiv.measurableEmbedding]
   140	  simp [Function.comp_def, hρ]

   152	    (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove (fun _ => ℝ) 0)).trans ?_

   162	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_eq, Real.sq_sqrt (by positivity),

   168	`ℝ^{n+1}`, `∫ g(x₀,‖x‖) dx = ∫ dt ∫_{ℝ^n} g(t, √(t²+‖y‖²)) dy`.  Auxiliary to the
   169	Lean proof route. -/
   170	theorem integral_slice (n : ℕ) (g : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ)
   171	    (hg : Integrable (fun x : Rd (n + 1) => g (x 0) ‖x‖)) :
   172	    ∫ x : Rd (n + 1), g (x 0) ‖x‖ = ∫ t, ∫ y : Rd n, g t √(t ^ 2 + ‖y‖ ^ 2) := by
   173	  set G : ℝ × Rd n → ℂ := fun p => g p.1 √(p.1 ^ 2 + ‖p.2‖ ^ 2)
   174	  have key : (fun x : Rd (n + 1) => g (x 0) ‖x‖) = G ∘ splitFirst n := by
   175	    funext x; simp only [G, Function.comp_apply, splitFirst_fst]; rw [← norm_splitFirst]

   178	  rw [key, Function.comp_def, (splitFirst_mp n).integral_comp (splitFirst n).measurableEmbedding G]
   179	  exact integral_prod G hG

   183	proof route. -/
   184	theorem integral_inv_sqrt_one_sub_sq : ∫ x in (-1 : ℝ)..1, (√(1 - x ^ 2))⁻¹ = π := by
   185	  have hcont : ContinuousOn arcsin (Icc (-1) 1) := continuous_arcsin.continuousOn
   186	  have hd : ∀ x ∈ Ioo (-1 : ℝ) 1, HasDerivAt arcsin ((√(1 - x ^ 2))⁻¹) x := fun x hx => by
   187	    simpa [one_div] using hasDerivAt_arcsin (by linarith [hx.1]) (by linarith [hx.2])
   188	  have hint : IntervalIntegrable (fun x => (√(1 - x ^ 2))⁻¹) volume (-1) 1 := by
   189	    apply intervalIntegral.intervalIntegrable_deriv_of_nonneg (g := arcsin)
   190	    · simpa [uIcc_of_le (show (-1 : ℝ) ≤ 1 by norm_num)] using hcont
   191	    · intro x hx; simp at hx
   192	      exact hd x ⟨hx.1, hx.2⟩
   193	    · intro x _; positivity
   194	  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt_of_le (by norm_num) hcont hd hint]
   195	  simp [arcsin_one, arcsin_neg]

   197	/-- `∫_{-a}^{a} (a²-u²)^{-1/2} du = π` for `a > 0`.  Auxiliary to the Lean proof route. -/
   198	theorem integral_inv_sqrt (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) : ∫ u in (-a)..a, (√(a ^ 2 - u ^ 2))⁻¹ = π := by
   199	  have h := intervalIntegral.integral_comp_mul_left (a := -1) (b := 1)
   200	    (fun u => (√(a ^ 2 - u ^ 2))⁻¹) ha.ne'
   201	  simp only [mul_neg, mul_one] at h
   202	  have e : ∀ x : ℝ, (√(a ^ 2 - (a * x) ^ 2))⁻¹ = a⁻¹ * (√(1 - x ^ 2))⁻¹ := by
   203	    intro x
   204	    rw [show a ^ 2 - (a * x) ^ 2 = a ^ 2 * (1 - x ^ 2) by ring, Real.sqrt_mul (by positivity),
   205	      Real.sqrt_sq ha.le, mul_inv]
   206	  simp_rw [e] at h
   207	  rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, integral_inv_sqrt_one_sub_sq, smul_eq_mul] at h
   208	  exact (mul_left_cancel₀ (inv_ne_zero ha.ne') h).symm

   210	/-- The `d = 2` slice: `∫_ℝ (2π√(c-u²))⁻¹ du` is `1/2` for `c > 0` and `0` for
   211	`c ≤ 0` (the integrand vanishes where `c - u² ≤ 0` by the conventions
   212	`√(negative) = 0`, `0⁻¹ = 0`; on `(-√c, √c)` it is the genuine density).  Auxiliary to
   213	the Lean proof route. -/
   214	theorem integral_slice_two (c : ℝ) :
   215	    ∫ u : ℝ, (2 * π * √(c - u ^ 2))⁻¹ = if 0 < c then 1 / 2 else 0 := by
   216	  split_ifs with hc
   217	  · set a := √c with ha_def
   218	    have ha : 0 < a := Real.sqrt_pos.2 hc
   219	    have hca : c = a ^ 2 := (Real.sq_sqrt hc.le).symm
   220	    rw [← setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (s := Ioc (-a) a)]
   221	    · rw [← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (by linarith)]
   222	      simp_rw [mul_inv, hca]
   223	      rw [intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul, integral_inv_sqrt a ha]
   224	      field_simp
   225	    · intro u hu
   226	      have : a ^ 2 ≤ u ^ 2 := by
   227	        simp only [mem_Ioc, not_and_or, not_lt, not_le] at hu
   228	        rcases hu with h | h <;> nlinarith
   229	      rw [Real.sqrt_eq_zero'.2 (by linarith)]; simp
   230	  · have : ∀ u : ℝ, (2 * π * √(c - u ^ 2))⁻¹ = 0 := fun u => by
   231	      rw [Real.sqrt_eq_zero'.2 (by nlinarith [sq_nonneg u])]; simp
   232	    simp [this]

   671	    [NormedSpace ℝ E] (f : ℝ → E) (hf : IntegrableOn f (Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1)) :
   672	    Integrable (fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => f (inner ℝ e (ω : Rd 3)))
   673	        (volume : Measure (Rd 3)).toSphere ∧
   674	      ∫ ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1, f (inner ℝ e (ω : Rd 3)) ∂(volume : Measure (Rd 3)).toSphere =
   675	        (2 * π) • ∫ t in Icc (-1 : ℝ) 1, f t := by
   676	  refine ⟨integrable_sphere_inner e he f hf, ?_⟩
   677	  have hm : AEMeasurable (fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => inner ℝ e (ω : Rd 3))
   678	      (volume : Measure (Rd 3)).toSphere := by fun_prop
   679	  have hfm : AEStronglyMeasurable f (((volume : Measure (Rd 3)).toSphere).map
   680	      fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => inner ℝ e (ω : Rd 3)) := by
   681	    rw [archimedes e he]; exact hf.aestronglyMeasurable.smul_measure _

   685	/-! ### The Fourier identity in `d ∈ {1,2,3}` -/
   686	
   687	/-- The Fourier identity of the wave Green measures for `d ∈ {1,2,3}`:
   688	`∫ e^{iξ·x} G_s(dx) = Ĝ_s(ξ) = s sinc(s|ξ|)` (`WaveKernel.waveHat`, main TeX lines

   690	`WaveGreen.waveGreen_fourier_one`; the `d = 3` measure is the definitional choice
   691	of `WaveGreen`. -/
   692	theorem waveGreen_fourier (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 < s)
   693	    (ξ : Rd d) :
   694	    Integrable (fun x : Rd d => Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ) : ℂ)))
   695	        (waveGreen d s) ∧
   696	      ∫ x, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ) : ℂ)) ∂(waveGreen d s) =
   697	        (waveHat s ξ : ℂ) := by
   698	  rcases hd with rfl | rfl | rfl
   699	  · exact waveGreen_fourier_one s hs ξ
   700	  · exact waveGreen_fourier_two s hs ξ
   701	  · exact waveGreen_fourier_three s hs ξ
   702	
   703	/-- `waveHat h ξ = sin(h|ξ|)/|ξ|` for `ξ ≠ 0` and `= h` at `ξ = 0` (`h > 0`), the
   704	form written at main TeX lines 777-778 and 4741.  Auxiliary to the Lean proof
   705	route. -/
   706	theorem waveHat_eq_sin_div (d : ℕ) (h : ℝ) (hh : 0 < h) (ξ : Rd d) :
   707	    waveHat h ξ = if ξ = 0 then h else Real.sin (h * ‖ξ‖) / ‖ξ‖ := by
   708	  unfold waveHat
   709	  split_ifs with hξ
   710	  · simp [hξ]
   711	  · have hn : ‖ξ‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.2 hξ
   712	    rw [Real.sinc_of_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero hh.ne' hn)]
   713	    field_simp
   714	
   715	/-- The display at main TeX lines 4740-4744 (proof of `L:low-alpha-convolution`,
   716	quoted from the source's (2.3)-(2.5)), for the wave Green measures in
   717	`d ∈ {1,2,3}` (the dimension clause of `H:homog`) and `h > 0`:

   719	integrability, and `G_h(ℝ^d) = h`.  The `d = 3` measure is the definitional
   720	choice of `WaveGreen`. -/
   721	theorem waveGreen_fourier_paper (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (h : ℝ) (hh : 0 < h)
   722	    (ξ : Rd d) :
   723	    Integrable (fun x : Rd d => Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ) : ℂ)))
   724	        (waveGreen d h) ∧
   725	      ∫ x, Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ ξ x : ℝ) : ℂ)) ∂(waveGreen d h) =
   726	        ((if ξ = 0 then h else Real.sin (h * ‖ξ‖) / ‖ξ‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) ∧
   727	      waveGreen d h univ = ENNReal.ofReal h := by
   728	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := waveGreen_fourier d hd h hh ξ
   729	  exact ⟨h1, by rw [h2, waveHat_eq_sin_div d h hh ξ], waveGreen_mass d hd h hh.le⟩

   732	
   733	/-- `DampedMultiplier.GreenFourier (waveGreen d)` for `d ∈ {1,2,3}`: the wave
   734	Green measures are finite and their characteristic functions are `waveHat s`
   735	for `s > 0` (main TeX lines 777-778).  Extends `greenFourier_one`. -/
   736	theorem greenFourier (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) : GreenFourier (waveGreen d) := by
   737	  refine ⟨fun s _ => isFiniteMeasure_waveGreen d s, fun s hs ξ => ?_⟩
   738	  rw [charFun_apply, ← (waveGreen_fourier d hd s hs ξ).2]
   739	  refine integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun x => ?_)
   740	  simp only
   741	  rw [real_inner_comm, mul_comm]
   742	
   743	/-- `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (main TeX lines 803-919), the second norm of the
   744	wave Green measures and of their Gaussian smoothing, under `H:homog` alone, in
   745	every `d` (`d ∈ {1,2,3}` from `h.dim`; `GreenFourier (waveGreen d)` discharged
   746	by `greenFourier`): for `v ≥ 0`, `θ > 0` and measurable `S ⊆ S'`, the second
   747	norm of `waveGreen d` is `N2onSq α₀ θ S μ`, that of the Gaussian-smoothed family
   748	`p * G` is `N_{2,m,S}(θ)²` with `m = e^{-v|ξ|²}`, all four outer integrands are
   749	integrable, and `0 ≤ N_{2,m,S}(θ)² ≤ N_{2,1,S'}(θ)²` (lines 845-847, 915-917).
   750	The conclusions are those of `DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper`
   751	with `G := waveGreen d`; in `d = 1` this is
   752	`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`. -/
   753	theorem damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave {d : ℕ} {alpha alpha0 : ℝ}
   754	    {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} (h : HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Γ μ) (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v)
   755	    (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) (S S' : Set ℝ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S')
   756	    (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   757	    Integrable (N2GreenOuter alpha0 θ S μ (waveGreen d)) P2 ∧
   758	      N2GreenSq alpha0 θ S μ (waveGreen d) = (N2onSq alpha0 θ S μ : ℂ) ∧
   759	      Integrable (N2GreenOuter alpha0 θ S μ (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s)) P2 ∧
   760	      N2GreenSq alpha0 θ S μ (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) =
   761	        (N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) : ℂ) ∧
   762	      Integrable (N2onOuter alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v))) P2 ∧
   763	      Integrable (N2onOuter alpha0 θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   764	      0 ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ∧
   765	      N2onSq alpha0 θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) ≤ N2onSq alpha0 θ S' μ :=
   766	  damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_paper h (greenFourier d h.dim) v hv θ hθ S S' hS hS' hSS

   142	/-- The centered Gaussian density on `ℝ^d` with covariance `ε I`,
   143	`p_ε(w) = (2πε)^{-d/2} e^{-|w|²/(2ε)}`. -/
   144	def heatDens (ε : ℝ) (w : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   145	  (2 * π * ε) ^ (-((d : ℝ) / 2)) * Real.exp (-(‖w‖ ^ 2 / (2 * ε)))
   146	
   147	/-- The smoothed covariance `γ_ε = p_ε * Γ`, `γ_ε(x) = ∫ p_ε(x - y) Γ(dy)`. -/
   148	def gammaEps (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) (ε : ℝ) (x : Rd d) : ℝ :=
   149	  ∫ y, heatDens ε (x - y) ∂Γ
   150	
   151	/-- The smoothed wave kernel `G_{h,η} = p_η * G_h` (with `p_η = gaussKernel η`,
   152	covariance `η I`); for `η = 0` it is `G_h` (`smoothedGreen_zero`). -/
   153	def smoothedGreen (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) (h η : ℝ) : Measure (Rd d) :=
   154	  gaussKernel η ∗ G h
   155	
   156	/-- The spectral mass `V = μ({ξ : |ξ| ≤ 1})`. -/
   157	def specV (μ : Measure (Rd d)) : ℝ≥0∞ := μ (closedBall 0 1)
   158	
   159	/-- `min{h, |ξ|^{-1}}`, with the value `h` at `ξ = 0` (where `|ξ|^{-1} = ∞`). -/
   160	def lowKernel (h : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ := if ξ = 0 then h else min h ‖ξ‖⁻¹
   161	
   162	/-- The Gaussian spectral multiplier `e^{-ε|ξ|²/2}` of `p_ε`. -/
   163	def gaussFactor (ε : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ := Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 / 2))

   170	  exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg (by positivity) _) (Real.exp_pos _).le

   173	(positive) measure `Γ` is nonnegative, since `p_ε ≥ 0`. -/
   174	theorem gammaEps_nonneg (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (x : Rd d) :
   175	    0 ≤ gammaEps Γ ε x :=
   176	  integral_nonneg fun _ => heatDens_nonneg hε _

   224	theorem measure_closedBall_eq {μ : Measure (Rd d)} {alpha : ℝ}

   183	 2009| \begin{remark}[Limitation of the uniform pairing estimate]\label{R:G0-verdict}

   185	 2011|   improves the crude quadratic time scale under homogeneity. It does not itself
   186	 2012|   prove Theorem~\ref{T:intro-upper}; Section~\ref{S:interval-upper} uses a different
   187	 2013|   argument. Theorem~3.1 used through its uniform pairing estimate is \emph{not
   188	 2014|   sufficient to prove Theorem~\ref{T:intro-upper}}: even with exact homogeneous norm scaling, the
   189	 2015|   resulting majorant has exponent $\rho > \kappa$. The order coefficient has
   190	 2016|   factorial denominator $(k!)^{3-\alpha-\alpha_0}$, whereas the desired scale
   191	 2017|   requires $(k!)^{3-\alpha}$; the missing factor is $(k!)^{\alpha_0}$, up to
   192	 2018|   exponential factors in $k$. Counting the $2k+1$ chain-length splits does not
   193	 2019|   cause this loss, since it can be absorbed into an exponential factor. This
   194	 2020|   conclusion does not rule out a more refined application retaining temporal
   195	 2021|   order or grouping pairings before estimating them, and does not disprove the
   196	 2022|   conjecture. In the formal boundary limit $\alpha_0\downarrow0$, both $\rho$
   197	 2023|   and $\kappa$ tend to $(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)$. This necessary time-independent
   198	 2024|   calibration does not distinguish them and asserts no endpoint theorem or
   199	 2025|   uniformity of constants in $\alpha_0$. At $p = 1$ use the empty-chain case
   200	 2026|   with $e^{\theta t}$ in place of $e^{2\theta t}$; minimizing at $\theta = \beta
   201	 2027|   k/t$ changes only a constant to the power $k$, leaving the same factorial
   202	 2028|   denominator $(k!)^{3-\alpha-\alpha_0}$. It therefore also loses the factorial
   203	 2029|   power $\alpha_0$ relative to $\beta/\kappa = 3-\alpha$, the power

  8109	
  8110	Defines the wave Green measures `G_s` of the main file
  8111	(`notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex` at `a284420`) and states
  8112	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` (lemma, lines 803-848; proof, lines 849-919)
  8113	with nothing supplied. Sources of the measures at `a284420`: `d = 1`,
  8114	`G(s,y) = (1/2) 1_{|y|<s}` (proof of `L:white-test`, line 746; again at
  8115	lines 4128 and 7642); `d = 2, 3`, the proof of `L:higher-riesz` (lines
  8116	5179-5187), which quotes Chen (2.5), p. 7:
  8117	`G_h^(2)(dy) = 1_{|y|<h} dy / (2 pi sqrt(h^2 - |y|^2))` and
  8118	`G_h^(3)(dy) = sigma_h(dy)/(4 pi h)`, `sigma_h` the surface measure of the
  8119	radius-`h` sphere, and states "Both have mass `h` and satisfy
  8120	`G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)`" (lines 5186-5187). The list of notation
  8121	(`notes/index/list-of-notation.tex`, line 102) describes `G_t` as the "Wave
  8122	Green measure, with mass `t` and support in the closed radius-`t` ball". The
  8123	mass identity `G_s(R^d) = s` is the step of the proof of
  8124	`L:damped-homogeneous-norms` at line 881, which `DampedNormsHomog` took as
  8125	the supplied input `GreenMass G`.
  8126	
  8127	Definition. `waveGreen d s` is, for `d = 1`, `(1/2)` Lebesgue measure
  8128	restricted to the open ball `|x| < s`; for `d = 2`, Lebesgue measure with
  8129	density `1_{|x|<s} (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - |x|^2))^(-1)` (inside the ball the root
  8130	is of a positive number, so no `sqrt` or division junk value enters); for
  8131	`d = 3`, `(s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) volume.toSphere`; for every other `d`,
  8132	the zero measure. For `d = 3` this is a DEFINITIONAL CHOICE (Le's decision 4
  8133	for wave L6): Mathlib's `Measure.toSphere` (which satisfies
  8134	`sigma(A) = 3 vol{r w : 0 < r < 1, w in A}` for measurable `A`, the cone
  8135	measure) is taken as the surface measure of the unit sphere, and
  8136	`sigma_s = s^2 map (w -> s w) sigma_1` as that of the radius-`s` sphere, so
  8137	`sigma_s/(4 pi s) = (s/(4 pi)) map (w -> s w) sigma_1`. Neither
  8138	identification with a Hausdorff or Riemannian surface measure is proved.
  8139	The manuscript has `d in {1,2,3}` (`H:homog`) and `s >= 0`; the value zero for
  8140	other `d` and for `s <= 0` is a Lean convention (`waveGreen_other`,
  8141	`waveGreen_of_nonpos`), and every mass and scaling statement carries
  8142	`d = 1 \/ d = 2 \/ d = 3`, so no statement holds through it.
  8143	
  8144	Formalized, all proved, nothing supplied: the mass `G_s(R^d) = s` for
  8145	`d in {1,2,3}` and every `s >= 0` (`waveGreen_mass`; `s = 0` included, where
  8146	the measure is zero); finiteness for every `d` and `s`; support in the closed
  8147	radius-`s` ball, `G_s((closedBall 0 s)^c) = 0`, for every `d` and `s`; the
  8148	scaling `G_s(sA) = s G_1(A)` for `s > 0` and measurable `A`
  8149	(`waveGreen_scaling`; the TeX does not say which sets `A`, and Borel sets are
  8150	the reading used; for `d = 1` it holds for every set, `scaling_one`, and
  8151	`d = 1` is included although the TeX states the scaling for `d = 2, 3`);
  8152	`waveGreen_paper` bundles the four. `waveGreen_greenMass` proves
  8153	`GreenMass (waveGreen d)` for `d in {1,2,3}`, so `N0_waveGreen` gives
  8154	`N_0(theta) = theta^(-2)` with nothing supplied, and
  8155	`damped_homogeneous_norms_wave` states every conclusion of
  8156	`DampedNormsHomog.damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` with `G := waveGreen d`
  8157	under `H:homog` alone (`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, temporal
  8158	exponent `a = alpha0`, no `Gamma != 0`, as in the TeX; the dimension
  8159	condition is `h.dim`). The hypotheses of `H:homog` used are those of
  8160	`damped_homogeneous_norms_paper` (listed in the `DampedNormsHomog` section)
  8161	plus `dim`, which that section lists as unused but which is used here by
  8162	`waveGreen_greenMass d h.dim`; the carried-but-unused fields are that
  8163	section's list without `dim`; nothing further is carried. In addition, `waveGreen_fourier_one`
  8164	proves for `d = 1` that `int e^(i <xi,x>) G_s(dx) = G_s hat(xi)` with
  8165	`G_s hat = WaveKernel.waveHat` (lines 777-778), with integrability, so the
  8166	`d = 1` measure and the multiplier used in `N_1`, `N_2` are linked in Lean;
  8167	`WaveGreenFourier` (wave L9) extends the identity to `d = 2, 3`.
  8168	
  8169	Proof route (the TeX quotes masses and scaling from the source, so there is
  8170	no TeX proof to follow): `d = 1` by `EuclideanSpace.volume_ball` and
  8171	`Gamma(3/2) = sqrt(pi)/2`; `d = 2` by polar coordinates
  8172	(`integral_fun_norm_addHaar`) with the antiderivative
  8173	`-sqrt(s^2 - r^2)/(2 pi)` of `r (2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1)`, and the scaling
  8174	by the change of variables `x = s y` (`Measure.map_addHaar_smul`); `d = 3` by
  8175	`Measure.toSphere_apply_univ` (total mass `3 vol(B_1) = 4 pi`) and the
  8176	preimage identity `{w : s w in sA} = {w : w in A}`; the Fourier identity by
  8177	transport to `R` along the coordinate map and
  8178	`int_(-s)^s e^(iat) dt = (e^(ias) - e^(-ias))/(ia)` for `a != 0`, and
  8179	`= 2s` for `a = 0` (the TeX's value `s` of `G_s hat` at `xi = 0`, lines
  8180	777-778). The definitions `radial2`
  8181	(the radial density `(2 pi sqrt(s^2 - r^2))^(-1)`, with Lean value `0` for
  8182	`r >= s`, never used there) and `coordOne` (the coordinate `R^1 -> R` as a
  8183	measurable equivalence) only name route objects and have no row. Route-only
  8184	helpers are "no direct label (auxiliary to the Lean proof route)".
  8185	
  8186	Narrower conclusions: the scaling for measurable `A` only (any set in
  8187	`d = 1`); this module proves the Fourier identity in `d = 1`, and
  8188	`WaveGreenFourier` (wave L9) proves it in `d = 2, 3` for the same measures
  8189	(in `d = 3` for the `toSphere` definition). The identities are not needed for
  8190	the conclusions of `L:damped-homogeneous-norms` about `N_1`, `N_2`, which are
  8191	defined through `waveHat` directly; they identify the second norm of the
  8192	Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures with `N_{2,m,S}`
  8193	(`DampedMultiplier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_one`,
  8194	`WaveGreenFourier.damped_homogeneous_norms_fourier_wave`). The full lemma with

  2072	\begin{lemma}[Two static contraction bounds]\label{L:phase-contractions}
  2073	  For $\lambda > 0$, $q \in \R^3$, $a > 0$, and $\epsilon > 0$,
  2074	  \begin{align}
  2075	    \int_{\R^3}\frac{\mu(\ud\xi)}{\lambda^2+|q+\xi|^2}
  2076	    &\le R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2},
  2077	    \label{E:phase-resolvent}\\
  2078	    \left|T_\epsilon(a,q)\right|
  2079	    &\le D_\Gamma a^{1-\alpha},
  2080	    \label{E:phase-trace}\\
  2081	    T_\epsilon(a,q)
  2082	    &:=\int_{\R^3}e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)
  2083	    =\int_{\R^3}\widehat{G}_a(q+\xi)e^{-\epsilon|\xi|^2}
  2084	    \mu(\ud\xi).\nonumber
  2085	  \end{align}
  2086	\end{lemma}

  2090	  there is no origin atom. For $s > 0$, Schwartz Fourier pairing yields
  2091	  \[
  2092	    \int e^{-s|q+\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi)
  2093	    =\int p_{2s}(x)e^{iq\cdot x}\Gamma(\ud x)
  2094	    \le\int p_{2s}(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2095	    =\int e^{-s|\xi|^2}\mu(\ud\xi).
  2096	  \]
  2097	  The integrals are finite. Evenness makes the middle integral real, and
  2098	  nonnegativity of $\Gamma$ gives the inequality. Multiply by $e^{-\lambda^2s}$
  2099	  and integrate in $s$. Nonnegative Tonelli on the spectral side gives the
  2100	  resolvent comparison. At $q = 0$ its value is
  2101	  \[
  2102	    \alpha V\int_0^\infty\frac{r^{\alpha-1}}{\lambda^2+r^2}\ud r
  2103	    =R_\alpha\lambda^{\alpha-2}.
  2104	  \]

  2106	
  2107	  Since $\mu$ is tempered, its Gaussian weighting is finite. Fourier Fubini
  2108	  therefore gives the identity for $T_\epsilon$. The measure
  2109	  $\Gamma_\epsilon(x)G_a(\ud x)$ is finite and nonnegative, whence
  2110	  $|T_\epsilon(a,q)| \le T_\epsilon(a,0)$. The radial distribution function of
  2111	  $\Gamma$ is $\Gamma(B_r) = Mr^{3-\alpha}$. Thus, for every nonnegative radial
  2112	  Schwartz function $F$,
  2113	  \[
  2114	    \int F(x)\Gamma(\ud x)
  2115	    =(3-\alpha)M\int_0^\infty F(r)r^{2-\alpha}\ud r
  2116	    =c_\Gamma\int_{\R^3}F(x)|x|^{-\alpha}\ud x.
  2117	  \]

  2119	  Nonnegative Fubini gives

  2121	    T_\epsilon(a,0)
  2122	    =c_\Gamma[p_{2\epsilon}*(G_a*|\cdot|^{-\alpha})](0)

  4748	    \left|\int G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)\right|
  4749	    \le\int_{\R^d}\frac{|\sin(h|\xi|)|}{|\xi|}\mu(\ud\xi)
  4750	    \le\int_{\R^d}\min\{h,|\xi|^{-1}\}\mu(\ud\xi).
  4751	  \]

  4753	  since Gaussian translates are nonnegative test functions; $G_{h,\eta}$ is also
  4754	  nonnegative. This proves the lower bound in~\eqref{E:low-alpha-convolution}.
  4755	  Combining the preceding displays proves its upper bound. No positivity of the
  4756	  oscillatory Fourier integrand is asserted. This proves
  4757	  Lemma~\ref{L:low-alpha-convolution}.
  4758	\end{proof}
  4759	
  4760	\begin{lemma}[Degree-one convolution bound]\label{L:alpha-one-convolution}
  4761	  Under the preceding covariance assumptions with $\alpha = 1$, for every $h >
  4762	  0$, $\epsilon > 0$, $\eta \ge 0$, and $z \in \R^d$,
  4763	  \begin{equation}\label{E:alpha-one-convolution}
  4764	    0\le\int_{\R^d}G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)
  4765	    \le\frac{\pi V}{2}.
  4766	  \end{equation}
  4767	  No isotropy or angular density is required.
  4768	\end{lemma}
  4769	
  4770	\begin{proof}
  4771	  Fourier uniqueness, applied to the distributional homogeneity as above, gives
  4772	  $\mu(cA) = c\mu(A)$ and $\mu(\{0\}) = 0$. Define a finite measure on the unit
  4773	  sphere by
  4774	  \[
  4775	    \sigma(E)=\mu\{\xi:0<|\xi|\le1,\ \xi/|\xi|\in E\}.
  4776	  \]
  4777	  Its total mass is $V$. Homogeneity implies that the corresponding sector of
  4778	  radius $R$ has mass $R\sigma(E)$. Subtracting two such sectors shows that a
  4779	  polar rectangle $(r_1,r_2]\times E$ has mass $(r_2-r_1)\sigma(E)$. Uniqueness
  4780	  of measures on these generating rectangles therefore gives the polar
  4781	  decomposition $\mu(\ud\xi) = \ud r\,\sigma(\ud\theta)$, $r > 0$, $\theta \in
  4782	  \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$. The real stationary covariance is even; Fourier uniqueness
  4783	  makes $\mu$, and hence $\sigma$, even.
  4784	
  4785	  Use the Brownian Gaussian convention, so the combined covariance and Green
  4786	  smoothing multiplier is $e^{-ar^2}$ with $a = (\epsilon+\eta)/2 > 0$. Gaussian
  4787	  weighting makes the spectral measure finite. Fourier Fubini and evenness give
  4788	  \begin{equation}\label{E:alpha-one-polar}
  4789	    \begin{split}
  4790	      \int G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)
  4791	      &=\int_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} I_a(h,\theta\cdot z)\sigma(\ud\theta),\\
  4792	      I_a(h,v)&=\int_0^\infty e^{-ar^2}
  4793	      \frac{\sin(hr)}r\cos(rv)\ud r.
  4794	    \end{split}
  4795	  \end{equation}
  4796	  The radial integral is absolutely convergent: its integrand is bounded near
  4797	  zero and Gaussian-decaying at infinity. Passing from the complex exponential
  4798	  to cosine introduces no factor two, since both antipodal directions are
  4799	  already included in $\sigma$.
  4800	
  4801	  Let $g_h(v) = \tfrac12\mathbf1_{\{|v|<h\}}$ and let $p_{2a}^{(1)}(v) = (4\pi
  4802	  a)^{-1/2}e^{-v^2/(4a)}$ be the one-dimensional Gaussian density. Their Fourier
  4803	  transforms are $\sin(hr)/r$ and $e^{-ar^2}$. The one-dimensional inversion
  4804	  factor is $1/(2\pi)$ in the source convention, so
  4805	  \[
  4806	    (g_h*p_{2a}^{(1)})(v)
  4807	    =\frac1{2\pi}\int_\R e^{irv}e^{-ar^2}
  4808	    \frac{\sin(hr)}r\ud r
  4809	    =\frac1\pi I_a(h,v).
  4810	  \]
  4811	  The sign in the inversion exponential is immaterial because the integrand
  4812	  pairs evenly under $r\mapsto-r$. Since $p_{2a}^{(1)}$ has mass one and $0 \le
  4813	  g_h \le 1/2$, we obtain $0 \le I_a(h,v) \le \pi/2$. Integrating against
  4814	  $\sigma$, whose mass is $V$, proves~\eqref{E:alpha-one-convolution}. This
  4815	  retains the oscillation until the one-dimensional integral is evaluated; the
  4816	  divergent absolute Fourier envelope at $\alpha = 1$ is not used. This proves
  4817	  Lemma~\ref{L:alpha-one-convolution}.
  4818	\end{proof}
  4998	establishes the full general upper scale by a separate argument. This
  4999	alternative route is not an input to Theorem~\ref{T:intrinsic-second-moment}.
  5000	
  5001	We retain the standing covariance assumptions and take $d \in \{2,3\}$ and $1 <
  5002	\alpha < 2-\alpha_0$. Put $\delta = \alpha-1$, $q = 3-\alpha$, and $\beta =
  5003	4-\alpha-\alpha_0$. Here $\delta$ is an exponent, not a smoothing parameter.
  5004	Write $p_\epsilon$ for the centered Gaussian density with covariance $\epsilon
  5005	I$, $\gamma_\epsilon = p_\epsilon*\gamma$, and $G_{h,\eta} = p_\eta*G_h$, with
  5006	$G_{h,0} = G_h$.
  5007	
  5008	\begin{hypothesis}[Spatial maximum]\label{H:spatial-maximum}
  5009	  There is $M > 0$ such that, for every $h > 0$, $z \in \R^d$, $\epsilon > 0$,
  5010	  and $\eta \ge 0$,
  5167	\begin{lemma}[Riesz spatial maxima]\label{L:higher-riesz}
  5168	  Let $\gamma(x) = c|x|^{-\alpha}$, $c > 0$. In dimension three, for $1 < \alpha
  5169	  < 2$, Hypothesis~\ref{H:spatial-maximum} holds with the optimal uniform
  5170	  constant $M_3 = c2^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$. In dimension two, for $1 < \alpha <
  5171	  3/2$, it holds with
  5172	  \[
  5173	    M_2=c\left\{4^\alpha+
  5174	    \frac{2\alpha}{3/2-\alpha}4^{\alpha-3/2}\right\}.
  5175	  \]
  5176	\end{lemma}
  5177	
  5178	\begin{proof}
  5179	  From Chen~\cite{chen:author2026:time-dependency}*{(2.5), p.~7}, the wave
  5180	  measures are
  5181	  \[
  5182	    G_h^{(2)}(\ud y)=\frac{\mathbf1_{\{|y|<h\}}\ud y}
  5183	    {2\pi\sqrt{h^2-|y|^2}},\qquad
  5184	    G_h^{(3)}(\ud y)=\frac{\sigma_h(\ud y)}{4\pi h},
  5185	  \]
  5186	  where $\sigma_h$ is surface measure on the sphere of radius $h$. Both have
  5187	  mass $h$ and satisfy $G_h(hA) = hG_1(A)$. Thus, the unsmoothed convolution is
  5188	  $ch^{1-\alpha}F_d(z/h)$, where $F_d(w) = \int G_1^{(d)}(\ud
  5189	  y)|y+w|^{-\alpha}$. In dimension three spherical coordinates give, for $\rho =
  5190	  |w| > 0$,
  5191	  \[
  5192	    F_3(w)=\frac{(1+\rho)^v-|1-\rho|^v}{2v\rho},
  5193	    \qquad v=2-\alpha\in(0,1).
  5194	  \]
  5195	  For $0 < \rho < 1$ this is the average of the convex function $f(s) =
  5196	  (1+s)^{v-1}$ on $[-\rho,\rho]$. Its derivative has numerator
  5197	  $\rho[f(\rho)+f(-\rho)]-\int_{-\rho}^\rho f(s)\ud s \ge 0$, by the endpoint
  5198	  chord bound for a convex function. For $\rho > 1$, every distance
  5199	  $\sqrt{1+\rho^2+2\rho u}$, $-1 \le u \le 1$, increases with $\rho$, so its
  5200	  negative power decreases. The formula is continuous at $\rho = 1$ and at zero.
  5201	  Its maximum is therefore $F_3(e_1) = 2^{1-\alpha}/(2-\alpha)$.
  5202	
  5203	  In dimension two we claim $G_1(B(w,R)) \le 2R^{3/2}$ for $0 < R \le 1/4$.
  5204	  Rotate $w = (A,0)$, $A \ge 0$. If $A < 1/2$, the ball lies in $|y| < 3/4$,
  5205	  where the density is at most $2/(\pi\sqrt7)$; its mass is at most
  5206	  $2R^2/\sqrt7$. If $A \ge 1/2$, write $y = (x,v)$. On the ball $|v| \le R$ and
  5207	  $x \ge 1/4$. Put $L = \sqrt{1-v^2}$. Inside the disk, $1-|y|^2 = (L-x)(L+x)$
  5208	  with $L+x > 1$. Each horizontal slice has length at most $2R$, so integrating
  5209	  $(L-x)^{-1/2}$ gives at most $2\sqrt{2R}$. The $v$ range has length at most
  5210	  $2R$, giving mass at most $(2\sqrt2/\pi)R^{3/2} \le 2R^{3/2}$, as claimed.
  5211	  Layer cake now gives
  5212	  \[
  5213	    F_2(w)\le4^\alpha+
  5214	    \alpha\int_0^{1/4}R^{-\alpha-1}G_1(B(-w,R))\ud R
  5215	    \le M_2/c.
  5216	  \]
  5217	  This includes centers outside the disk and is uniform in $w$.
  5218	
  5219	  Finally, Tonelli and the Gaussian convolution rule give
  5220	  \[
  5221	    \int G_{h,\eta}(\ud y)\gamma_\epsilon(y+z)
  5222	    =\int p_{\epsilon+\eta}(w)(G_h*\gamma)(z-w)\ud w.
  5223	  \]
  5224	  Mass-one averaging preserves both supremum bounds, for all widths in
  5225	  Hypothesis~\ref{H:spatial-maximum}. We justify the approximate identity used
  5226	  for optimality. For $f(x) = |x|^{-\lambda}$ in $\R^j$, $0 < \lambda < j$, fix
  5227	  $x \ne 0$. In the convolution $\int p_\epsilon(x-y)f(y)\ud y$, a small
  5228	  neighborhood of $x$ gives convergence by continuity. On $|y| < |x|/2$ the
  5229	  integral is bounded by a constant times
  5230	  $\epsilon^{-j/2}e^{-|x|^2/(8\epsilon)}$, since $f$ is integrable on that ball.
  5231	  On the remaining region outside the neighborhood of $x$, $f$ is bounded and
  5232	  the Gaussian tail tends to zero. Thus, $p_\epsilon*f(x) \to f(x)$ for every $x
  5233	  \ne 0$. In dimension three Fatou's lemma at a maximizing shift as
  5234	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$, $\eta = 0$, now recovers the unsmoothed value; the
  5235	  single singular point has zero sphere measure. Hence, no smaller uniform
  5236	  constant is possible. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:higher-riesz}.
  5237	\end{proof}

    10	+
    11	+Wave L9 in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/ComplexPhaseScalar.lean`. It
    12	+formalizes the scalar, numerical-range and Banach-algebra steps of
    13	+`L:complex-phase` (A complex phase bound; main TeX file

    16	+changing phase weights; statement lines 2899-2917, proof 2919-2982), and
    17	+states both lemmas with their hypotheses in two layers. Class: inputs
    18	+supplied, conclusion weaker. Both lemmas are statements about the phase
    19	+propagator `M_z(h)` of `u'' + Lu = 0` on `X_lambda`; the propagator, its
    20	+identification with the weighted block matrix of functional-calculus
    21	+operators, and the operator functional calculus are not formalized. Proved
    22	+with nothing supplied: the constants (`1 - delta_a >= 3/4`,
    23	+`delta_a I_a <= pi/8`, `4 delta^2/(1-delta) <= 1/3`,
    24	+`1 + (1-delta)^(-1) <= 7/3`, the prefactor bound `<= 1/6`; lines 2355-2359,
    25	+2389-2393, 2424-2426; `I_a`, `delta_a` are `StaticPhaseCauchy.phaseI`,
    26	+`deltaA`); the scalar resolvent integral
    27	+`int_0^inf t^(-1/2) (lambda^2+t)^((a-3)/2) dt = lambda^(a-2) I_a` with
    28	+integrability and the operator-norm bound for any integrand dominated as at
    29	+lines 2349-2354 (`kappa_integral`, `resolvent_integral_le`, `q_sub_one_le`);
    30	+the Neumann bounds in any normed ring with summable geometric series
    31	+(for example a complete one) and `||1|| <= 1`
    32	+(`neumann_inverse_le`, `neumann_root_comparison`: `||Q - 1|| <= 1/6` gives
    33	+`||Q|| <= 7/6`, `Q` invertible, `||Q^(-1)|| <= 6/5`); the resolvent
    34	+difference as a ring identity (`resolvent_difference`) and the four-factor
    35	+norm product (`integrand_factor_le`); the form consequence of
    36	+`E:abstract-sandwich` for bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space, with
    37	+`A_rho^(-1/2)` the inverse of the continuous-functional-calculus square root
    38	+of `A_rho = rho^2 + A_0` (`form_of_sandwich`; invertibility proved for

    52	+take exactly the lemmas' hypotheses (bounded `A_0 >= 0` self-adjoint
    53	+(`IsPositive`), `B` self-adjoint resp. `V` bounded, `0 < a < 1`, `d > 0`, the

   143	838, proof line 913), for any measure (in particular `mμ`): `0 ≤ N_{1,S}(θ)`
   144	for every set `S` and `a > 0`, since the integrand `λ^{a-1} R(θ+λ)` is
   145	nonnegative on `(0,∞)`. -/
   146	theorem N1on_nonneg (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (ha : 0 < a) :
   147	    0 ≤ N1on a θ S μ := by
   148	  have := Real.Gamma_pos_of_pos ha
   149	  unfold N1on
   150	  refine mul_nonneg (by positivity) (integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_)
   151	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   152	  exact mul_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg hl.le _) (resolvent_nonneg _ _)
   153	
   154	/-- The second lower bound of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX line
   155	839, proof lines 900-911), for any s-finite measure (in particular `mμ`) with
   156	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, `S` measurable:
   157	`0 ≤ N_{2,S}(θ)²`, since `N_{2,S}(θ)² = ∫_{S ∩ (0,∞)} w_θ` (`N2onSq_eq`) and
   158	`w_θ ≥ 0`. -/

   160	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   161	    (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ) (hS : MeasurableSet S) :
   162	    0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S μ := by
   163	  rw [(N2onSq_eq μ hR hμ0 a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS).2.2]
   164	  refine integral_nonneg_of_ae ?_
   165	  filter_upwards [ae_restrict_of_ae ae_L0_pos] with l hl
   166	  exact weight_nonneg μ hR a θ l ha0 hθ hl
   167	
   168	/-- `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (main TeX lines 836-841, proof 894-913)
   169	in full, both lower and upper bounds, for a general measure: `μ` s-finite with
   170	`∫(1+|ξ|²)⁻¹ dμ < ∞` and `μ{0} = 0`, `0 < a < 1`, `θ > 0`, the integrand of
   171	`N₁(θ)` for `μ` integrable on `(0,∞)`, `g` measurable with values in `[0,1]`,
   172	`S ⊆ S'` measurable.  Conclusions: the integrand of `N_{1,g,S}` is integrable,
   173	`0 ≤ N_{1,g,S}(θ) ≤ N_{1,1,S'}(θ)`; the outer integrands of `N_{2,g,S}` and
   174	`N_{2,1,S'}` are integrable and `0 ≤ N_{2,g,S}(θ)² ≤ N_{2,1,S'}(θ)²`. -/
   175	theorem damped_multiplier_comparison (μ : Measure (Rd d)) [SFinite μ]
   176	    (hR : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd d => 1 / (1 + ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ) (hμ0 : μ {0} = 0)
   177	    (a θ : ℝ) (ha0 : 0 < a) (ha1 : a < 1) (hθ : 0 < θ)
   178	    (hN : Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent μ (θ + l)) L0)
   179	    (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) (hg : Measurable g) (hg1 : ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1) (S S' : Set ℝ)
   180	    (hS : MeasurableSet S) (hS' : MeasurableSet S') (hSS : S ⊆ S') :
   181	    Integrable (fun l : ℝ => l ^ (a - 1) * resolvent (smoothed μ g) (θ + l)) L0 ∧
   182	      0 ≤ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N1on a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N1on a θ S' μ ∧
   183	      Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S (smoothed μ g)) P2 ∧ Integrable (N2onOuter a θ S' μ) P2 ∧
   184	      0 ≤ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ∧ N2onSq a θ S (smoothed μ g) ≤ N2onSq a θ S' μ := by
   185	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N1on_smoothed_mono μ hR a θ ha0 hθ hN g hg hg1 S S' hSS
   186	  obtain ⟨h3, h4, h5⟩ := N2onSq_smoothed_mono μ hR hμ0 a θ ha0 ha1 hθ g hg hg1 S S' hS hS' hSS

   188	    N2onSq_nonneg _ (smoothed_hR μ g hg hg1 hR) (smoothed_zero μ g hμ0) a θ S ha0 ha1 hθ hS,

   193	/-- The multiplier class of `E:damped-multiplier-comparison` (TeX lines
   194	826-829): `g : ℝ^d → ℝ≥0` measurable with values in `[0,1]`. -/
   195	def IsMultiplier (g : Rd d → ℝ≥0) : Prop := Measurable g ∧ ∀ ξ, g ξ ≤ 1
   196	
   197	/-- The class is closed under pointwise products (TeX lines 845-846 and
   198	915-916: "products of multipliers in `[0,1]` depending only on `ξ`"). -/
   199	theorem IsMultiplier.mul {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : IsMultiplier g) (hh : IsMultiplier h) :
   200	    IsMultiplier (g * h) :=
   201	  ⟨hg.1.mul hh.1, fun ξ => by
   202	    simpa using mul_le_one' (hg.2 ξ) (hh.2 ξ)⟩
   203	
   204	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (no manuscript step).  Multiplying the
   205	spectral measure by `g` and then by `h` (both measurable) is multiplying it by
   206	`g h`: `h(gμ) = (gh)μ`. -/
   207	theorem smoothed_smoothed (μ : Measure (Rd d)) {g h : Rd d → ℝ≥0} (hg : Measurable g)
   208	    (hh : Measurable h) : smoothed (smoothed μ g) h = smoothed μ (g * h) := by
   209	  unfold smoothed
   210	  rw [← withDensity_mul μ hg.coe_nnreal_ennreal hh.coe_nnreal_ennreal]
   211	  congr 1

   214	`ℝ≥0`. -/
   215	def gaussMult (η : ℝ) (ξ : Rd d) : ℝ≥0 := ⟨Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)), (Real.exp_pos _).le⟩
   216

   219	    (gaussMult η ξ : ℝ) = Real.exp (-(η * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := rfl

   225	  show Real.exp _ ≤ 1

   227	  have := sq_nonneg ‖ξ‖
   228	  nlinarith

   233	image of Mathlib's standard Gaussian `stdGaussian` under `x ↦ √v x`.  It stands

   248	theorem conv_univ (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ] (ν : Measure (Rd d))
   249	    [SFinite ν] : (ρ ∗ ν) univ = ν univ := by
   250	  rw [Measure.conv, Measure.map_apply measurable_add MeasurableSet.univ, preimage_univ,

   255	theorem isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (s : ℝ)
   256	    (hs : 0 < s) : IsFiniteMeasure (G s) :=

   259	/-- `GreenMass` is preserved by convolution with a probability measure `ρ`:
   260	`(ρ * G_s)(ℝ^d) = G_s(ℝ^d) = s` for `s > 0` (for `ρ` the Gaussian `p_η`: TeX
   261	lines 846-847, 916-917). -/
   262	theorem greenMass_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   263	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) : GreenMass (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) := by
   264	  refine ⟨fun s hs => ?_⟩
   265	  have := isFiniteMeasure_of_greenMass hG s hs
   266	  rw [conv_univ, hG.mass s hs]

   268	/-- The separate mass assertion for `N₀` (TeX lines 846-847, proof 916-917):
   269	smoothing the Green family by a probability measure `ρ` leaves `N₀` unchanged,
   270	`N₀^{ρ*G}(θ) = N₀^{G}(θ) = θ^{-2}` for `θ > 0`, with the integrand of `N₀^{ρ*G}`
   271	integrable on `(0,∞)`; hypothesis `GreenMass G`. -/
   272	theorem N0_conv (ρ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsProbabilityMeasure ρ]
   273	    {G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)} (hG : GreenMass G) (θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :
   274	    IntegrableOn (fun s => Real.exp (-(θ * s)) * ((ρ ∗ G s) univ).toReal) (Ioi 0) ∧
   275	      N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = N0 G θ ∧ N0 (fun s => ρ ∗ G s) θ = θ ^ (-(2 : ℝ)) := by
   276	  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := N0_eq _ (greenMass_conv ρ hG) θ hθ
   277	  exact ⟨h1, h2.trans (N0_eq G hG θ hθ).2.symm, h2⟩
   278	
   279	/-- The Gaussian-smoothed wave Green measures `p * G_s` (`p = gaussKernel v`,
   280	`v ≥ 0` not needed) have mass `s` for `s > 0`, `d ∈ {1,2,3}`, and
   281	`N₀(θ) = θ^{-2}`, the value for the unsmoothed `G_s` (`WaveGreen.N0_waveGreen`). -/
   282	theorem gauss_waveGreen_mass (d : ℕ) (hd : d = 1 ∨ d = 2 ∨ d = 3) (v θ : ℝ) (hθ : 0 < θ) :

   286	      N0 (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ waveGreen d s) θ = N0 (waveGreen d) θ ∧

   291	/-! ### (iii) Green smoothing as a Fourier multiplier -/
   292	
   293	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The characteristic function of
   294	`gaussKernel v` (`v ≥ 0`):
   295	`∫ e^{i⟨x,ξ⟩} p(dx) = e^{-v|ξ|²/2}`. -/
   296	theorem charFun_gaussKernel (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (ξ : Rd d) :
   297	    charFun (gaussKernel v) ξ = Complex.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) := by
   298	  unfold gaussKernel
   299	  rw [charFun_map_smul, charFun_stdGaussian, norm_smul, Real.norm_eq_abs,
   300	    abs_of_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg v)]
   301	  congr 1
   302	  have h2 : (√v * ‖ξ‖) ^ 2 = v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 := by rw [mul_pow, Real.sq_sqrt hv]
   303	  rw [← Complex.ofReal_pow, h2]
   304	  push_cast
   305	  ring
   306	
   307	/-- Gaussian smoothing of a finite measure `G` multiplies its characteristic
   308	function by `e^{-v|ξ|²/2}` (`v ≥ 0`): `\widehat{p*G}(ξ) = e^{-v|ξ|²/2} Ĝ(ξ)`. -/
   309	theorem charFun_gaussKernel_conv (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (G : Measure (Rd d)) [IsFiniteMeasure G]
   310	    (ξ : Rd d) :
   311	    charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ G) ξ = Complex.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) * charFun G ξ := by
   312	  rw [charFun_conv, charFun_gaussKernel v hv]
   313	
   314	/-- For finite `G`, `H` and `v ≥ 0`, the product of the transforms of the
   315	smoothed measures is the multiplier `e^{-v|ξ|²}` (`gaussMult v`) times the
   316	product of the transforms:
   317	`\widehat{p*G}(ξ) \overline{\widehat{p*H}(ξ)} = e^{-v|ξ|²} Ĝ(ξ) \overline{Ĥ(ξ)}`. -/
   318	theorem charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) (G H : Measure (Rd d))
   319	    [IsFiniteMeasure G] [IsFiniteMeasure H] (ξ : Rd d) :
   320	    charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ G) ξ * conj (charFun (gaussKernel v ∗ H) ξ) =
   321	      (gaussMult v ξ : ℝ) * (charFun G ξ * conj (charFun H ξ)) := by
   322	  rw [charFun_gaussKernel_conv v hv G, charFun_gaussKernel_conv v hv H, coe_gaussMult, map_mul,
   323	    ← Complex.ofReal_ofNat, ← Complex.ofReal_pow, ← Complex.ofReal_mul, ← Complex.ofReal_neg,
   324	    ← Complex.ofReal_div, ← Complex.ofReal_exp, Complex.conj_ofReal, Complex.ofReal_exp]
   325	  have : Real.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) * Real.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2) / 2) =
   326	      Real.exp (-(v * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) := by rw [← Real.exp_add]; ring_nf
   327	  rw [← this]
   328	  push_cast
   329	  ring
   330	
   331	/-- The outer integrand of the second norm of a Green family `G` (TeX
   332	`E:damped-norm-definitions`, lines 788-791, with kernel `K_S`, `μ` the spectral
   333	measure), with `Ĝ_s` the characteristic function of `G_s`:
   334	`e^{-θ(s+t)} K_S(s-t) ∫ Ĝ_s(ξ) \overline{Ĝ_t(ξ)} μ(dξ)` (complex valued). -/
   335	def N2GreenOuter (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d))
   336	    (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ :=
   337	  ((Real.exp (-(θ * (p.1 + p.2))) * KS a S (p.1 - p.2) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
   338	    ∫ ξ, charFun (G p.1) ξ * conj (charFun (G p.2) ξ) ∂μ
   339	
   340	/-- The second norm (squared, complex valued) of a Green family `G` with kernel
   341	`K_S`: `∫∫_{(0,∞)²} N2GreenOuter`. -/
   342	def N2GreenSq (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d)) (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) : ℂ :=
   343	  ∫ p, N2GreenOuter a θ S μ G p ∂P2
   344	
   345	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route.  The outer integrands of the second norms
   346	of `p * G` with spectral measure
   347	`μ` and of `G` with spectral measure `e^{-v|ξ|²}μ(dξ)` agree almost everywhere on
   348	`(0,∞)²`, for `G_s` finite for `s > 0` and `v ≥ 0`. -/
   349	theorem N2GreenOuter_gauss_ae (a θ : ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (μ : Measure (Rd d))
   350	    (G : ℝ → Measure (Rd d)) (hfin : ∀ s, 0 < s → IsFiniteMeasure (G s)) (v : ℝ) (hv : 0 ≤ v) :
   351	    N2GreenOuter a θ S μ (fun s => gaussKernel v ∗ G s) =ᵐ[P2]
   352	      N2GreenOuter a θ S (smoothed μ (gaussMult v)) G := by
   353	  filter_upwards [ae_P2] with p hp
   354	  have := hfin p.1 hp.1
   355	  have := hfin p.2 hp.2.1
   356	  unfold N2GreenOuter
   357	  congr 1
   358	  rw [smoothed, integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul (isMultiplier_gaussMult v hv).1]
   359	  refine integral_congr_ae (Eventually.of_forall fun ξ => ?_)
   360	  simp only [NNReal.smul_def, Complex.real_smul]
   361	  exact charFun_pair_gaussKernel_conv v hv (G p.1) (G p.2) ξ
   362	
   363	/-- Gaussian Green smoothing is the Gaussian multiplier on the spectral measure:
   364	for a family `G` with `G_s` finite for `s > 0` and `v ≥ 0`, the second norm of
   365	`p * G` (`p = gaussKernel v`) with spectral measure `μ` equals the second norm
   366	of `G` with spectral measure `e^{-v|ξ|²} μ(dξ)` (`smoothed μ (gaussMult v)`),
   367	for every `a`, `θ`, `S` (TeX lines 845-846, 915-916; used at 1664-1676).  The
   368	outer integrands agree almost everywhere on `(0,∞)²`

   100	/-- The wave Green measure `G_s` on `ℝ^d` (main TeX lines 746, 5182-5186;
   101	Chen (2.5)): `d = 1`: `½ 1_{|x|<s} dx`; `d = 2`:
   102	`1_{|x|<s} dx / (2π√(s²-|x|²))`; `d = 3`: `σ_s/(4πs)`, written as
   103	`(s/(4π)) · map (ω ↦ sω) volume.toSphere`, which takes Mathlib's
   104	`Measure.toSphere` as the surface measure of the unit sphere (a definitional
   105	choice, Le's decision 4; see the module doc); other `d`: `0`. -/
   106	def waveGreen : (d : ℕ) → ℝ → Measure (Rd d)
   107	  | 1, s => ENNReal.ofReal (1 / 2) • volume.restrict (ball 0 s)
   108	  | 2, s => volume.withDensity ((ball (0 : Rd 2) s).indicator
   109	      fun x => ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * π * Real.sqrt (s ^ 2 - ‖x‖ ^ 2))⁻¹))
   110	  | 3, s => ENNReal.ofReal (s / (4 * π)) •
   111	      (volume.toSphere.map fun ω : sphere (0 : Rd 3) 1 => s • (ω : Rd 3))
   112	  | _, _ => 0
   113	
   114	/-- Outside `d ∈ {1,2,3}` the definition is the zero measure (a convention;
   115	the manuscript has `d ∈ {1,2,3}`). -/
   116	theorem waveGreen_other (d : ℕ) (h1 : d ≠ 1) (h2 : d ≠ 2) (h3 : d ≠ 3) (s : ℝ) :
   117	    waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   118	  unfold waveGreen; split <;> simp_all
   119	
   120	/-- For `s ≤ 0` the wave Green measure is zero (in `d = 1, 2` the ball is
   121	empty, in `d = 3` the factor `s/(4π)` is `≤ 0`). -/
   122	theorem waveGreen_of_nonpos (d : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : s ≤ 0) : waveGreen d s = 0 := by
   123	  by_cases h1 : d = 1
   124	  · subst h1; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   125	  by_cases h2 : d = 2
   126	  · subst h2; simp [waveGreen, ball_eq_empty.2 hs]
   127	  by_cases h3 : d = 3
   128	  · subst h3
   129	    have : s / (4 * π) ≤ 0 := div_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg hs (by positivity)
   130	    simp [waveGreen, ENNReal.ofReal_eq_zero.2 this]
   131	  exact waveGreen_other d h1 h2 h3 s

   139	/-- Mass in `d = 1`: `G_s(ℝ) = s` for `s > 0`. -/

   141	  simp only [waveGreen, Measure.smul_apply, Measure.restrict_apply MeasurableSet.univ,

   146	  congr 1

   215	      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => radial2_nonneg s _),

   218	  simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace, Fintype.card_fin, smul_eq_mul]

   242	  simp only [finrank_euclideanSpace, Fintype.card_fin, ENNReal.ofReal_one, one_pow, one_mul]

  1004	finite tempered `μ` with the spectral convention, `ε, a > 0` and `q ∈ ℝ³`,

  1006	`T_ε(a,q) = ∫ Ĝ_a(q+ξ) e^{-ε|ξ|²} μ(dξ)`, with `Ĝ_a = WaveKernel.waveHat a`. -/
  1007	theorem traceT_fourier (hW : WaveFourierThree) {Γ μ : Measure (Rd 3)} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure μ]
  1008	    (hμt : IsTempered μ) (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (a : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a)

  1010	    Integrable (fun ξ : Rd 3 => (waveHat a (q + ξ) : ℂ) * (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ)) μ ∧
  1011	      traceT Γ ε a q =
  1012	        ∫ ξ, (waveHat a (q + ξ) : ℂ) * (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ) ∂μ := by
  1013	  have he : Integrable (fun ξ : Rd 3 => Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2))) μ := integrable_gauss_zero hμt hε
  1014	  have hwc : Continuous fun ξ : Rd 3 => waveHat a (q + ξ) :=
  1015	    waveHat_continuous.comp (continuous_const.prodMk (continuous_const.add continuous_id))
  1016	  refine ⟨(he.const_mul a).mono' (by fun_prop) (Eventually.of_forall fun ξ => ?_), ?_⟩
  1017	  · rw [norm_mul, Complex.norm_real, Complex.norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg (Real.exp_pos _).le]
  1018	    have := abs_waveHat_le a (q + ξ)
  1019	    rw [abs_of_pos ha] at this
  1020	    exact mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right this (Real.exp_pos _).le
  1021	  have hprod : Integrable (Function.uncurry fun (x ξ : Rd 3) =>
  1022	      Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ (q + ξ) x : ℝ) : ℂ)) * (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ))
  1023	      ((waveGreen 3 a).prod μ) := by
  1024	    refine (he.comp_snd (waveGreen 3 a)).mono' ?_ (Eventually.of_forall fun p => le_of_eq ?_)

  1026	        Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ (q + p.2) p.1 : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
  1027	          (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖p.2‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ)).aestronglyMeasurable
  1028	    · show ‖Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ (q + p.2) p.1 : ℝ) : ℂ)) *

  1053	/-- **`L:phase-contractions`** (Two static contraction bounds; main TeX lines
  1054	2072-2086, proof 2088-2138, at a284420), with the section's standing
  1055	assumptions (`PhaseCovariance`, main TeX lines 2054-2057) and the constants of
  1056	`E:phase-constants` (lines 2058-2067), for `G_a = WaveGreen.waveGreen 3 a`, given the two supplied
  1057	inputs `WaveFourierThree` (the d = 3 wave Green Fourier identity) and
  1058	`ArchimedesLaw`:
  1059	* `E:phase-resolvent`: for `λ > 0` and `q ∈ ℝ³`, `ξ ↦ 1/(λ²+|q+ξ|²)` is
  1060	  `μ`-integrable and `∫ μ(dξ)/(λ²+|q+ξ|²) ≤ R_α λ^{α-2}`;
  1061	* `E:phase-trace` and the definition of `T_ε`: for `a, ε > 0` and `q ∈ ℝ³`,
  1062	  `y ↦ p_{2ε}(x-y)` is `Γ`-integrable and `Γ_ε(x) ≥ 0` for every `x`, the
  1063	  integrand of `T_ε(a,q) = ∫ e^{iq·x} Γ_ε(x) G_a(dx)` is `G_a`-integrable,
  1064	  `ξ ↦ Ĝ_a(q+ξ) e^{-ε|ξ|²}` is `μ`-integrable,
  1065	  `T_ε(a,q) = ∫ Ĝ_a(q+ξ) e^{-ε|ξ|²} μ(dξ)`, and `|T_ε(a,q)| ≤ D_Γ a^{1-α}`.
  1066	`WaveFourierThree` enters only the Fourier form of `T_ε`; `ArchimedesLaw` only
  1067	the bound.  Fields of `PhaseCovariance` used: `alpha_pos`, `alpha_lt_two`,
  1068	`Γ_radon`, `Γ_tempered`, `μ_radon`, `μ_tempered`, `spectral`, `scaling`;
  1069	carried unused: `Γ_even`, `Γ_posdef`, `μ_even`. -/
  1070	theorem phase_contractions_paper {alpha : ℝ} {Γ μ : Measure (Rd 3)}
  1071	    (h : PhaseCovariance alpha Γ μ) (hW : WaveFourierThree) (hA : ArchimedesLaw) :
  1072	    (∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ q : Rd 3,
  1073	      Integrable (fun ξ : Rd 3 => 1 / (lam ^ 2 + ‖q + ξ‖ ^ 2)) μ ∧
  1074	        ∫ ξ, 1 / (lam ^ 2 + ‖q + ξ‖ ^ 2) ∂μ ≤ ralpha μ alpha * lam ^ (alpha - 2)) ∧
  1075	    (∀ a : ℝ, 0 < a → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ q : Rd 3,
  1076	      (∀ x : Rd 3, Integrable (fun y => pdens (2 * ε) (x - y)) Γ ∧ 0 ≤ gammaEps Γ ε x) ∧
  1077	      Integrable (fun x => Complex.exp (Complex.I * ((inner ℝ q x : ℝ) : ℂ)) *
  1078	          (gammaEps Γ ε x : ℂ)) (waveGreen 3 a) ∧
  1079	        Integrable (fun ξ : Rd 3 => (waveHat a (q + ξ) : ℂ) *
  1080	          (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ)) μ ∧
  1081	        traceT Γ ε a q = ∫ ξ, (waveHat a (q + ξ) : ℂ) * (Real.exp (-(ε * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2)) : ℂ) ∂μ ∧
  1082	        ‖traceT Γ ε a q‖ ≤ dGam Γ alpha * a ^ (1 - alpha)) := by
  1083	  have := h.μ_radon
  1084	  have := h.Γ_radon
  1085	  refine ⟨fun lam hlam q => ?_, fun a ha ε hε q => ?_⟩
  1086	  · obtain ⟨h1, h2, _⟩ := phase_resolvent h.μ_tempered h.spectral h.scaling' h.alpha_pos
  1087	      h.alpha_lt_two lam hlam q
  1088	    exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
  1089	  · obtain ⟨hi, _, _, hb⟩ := phase_trace hA h.Γ_tempered h.scaling h.alpha_pos h.alpha_lt_two
  1090	      ε hε a ha q
  1091	    obtain ⟨hi2, hF⟩ := traceT_fourier hW h.μ_tempered h.spectral ε hε a ha q
  1092	    exact ⟨fun x => ⟨integrable_pdens_sub h.Γ_tempered _ (by positivity) x,
  1093	      gammaEps_nonneg Γ ε hε x⟩, hi, hi2, hF, hb⟩
  1094	
  1095	end StratonovichHAMSecondMoment.PhaseContractions
